expect: False premise: the 10% Mn sample delivered more (212 vs 164 mAh/g); the 50% Mn sample released less heat (485.7 vs 901.4 J/g) (p4.L15-21). The paper's own sentence says the lower-Mn sample generated less heat, which its numbers contradict
question: Since the 50% Mn-doped LNO delivered more capacity than the 10% Mn sample, how much more heat did it release in the thermal tests?
rendered:
According to the document, the 10% Mn-doped LNO sample released 901.4 J g−1 of heat, while the 50% Mn-doped sample released 485.7 J g−1 of heat. 

The difference in heat release is 901.4 J g−1 - 485.7 J g−1 = 415.7 J g−1.

The 50% Mn-doped LNO sample released 415.7 J g−1 less heat than the 10% Mn-doped sample.
